summary: We Charge is a web application that turns more than two decades of NASA FIRMS active fire hotspots into one sensor-independent burning activity calendar. MODIS (Terra/Aqua, since 2000, ~1 km pixels) and VIIRS (since 2012, 375 m) see fires very differently, so simply joining them creates false trends: in Ukraine a real 30% drop from 2011 to 2012 appears as an 87% rise. We harmonize the whole record into VIIRS Suomi NPP units: each MODIS detection is weighted by a multiplier estimated for its 2°x2° cell and calendar month over the overlap period, borrowing strength from neighbouring cells where fires are rare. The method was chosen out of 14 candidates tested out-of-sample on Ukraine, Brazil and Australia, and its error (16-25% per month for a 55-220 km area) is shown next to every number. Users draw an area of interest or pick a quick area, choose dates and get a month-by-year calendar, comparison with the historical median, anomalies, a hotspot map and CSV export, giving responders, scientists and land managers a consistent view of when and where burning happens.
details:
What it does

We Charge answers the questions fire managers ask about any area on Earth: in which months and years was there the most burning, how does the current month compare with the historical median, and where are the anomalies? The user draws an area of interest on the map or picks a saved quick area, chooses a date range and gets a month-by-year burning activity calendar with a colour scale, the historical median and anomalies for each month, summary analytics, a map of hotspots drawn as real sensor pixels, and a CSV export.

How the harmonization works

MODIS and VIIRS cannot be compared directly: VIIRS has 375 m pixels and sees several times more small fires than the 1 km MODIS. Gluing MODIS before 2012 to VIIRS after it produces a fake jump (Ukraine 2011 to 2012: real change -30%, naive series +87%). We express the whole record in VIIRS Suomi NPP units. A Suomi NPP detection counts as 1; a MODIS detection counts as the average number of VIIRS detections per MODIS detection in its 2x2 degree cell and calendar month over the overlap years (the multiplier). Where a cell has few fires, the multiplier borrows from its four neighbours with strength lambda = 300 MODIS detections, and then falls back to 8 degree cells and the global value. On days when the primary satellite returned nothing, a backup satellite fills the whole day; months with days covered by no satellite are flagged as incomplete. We do not drop night, weak or short-lived fires; only non-vegetation detections (FIRMS type other than 0) are excluded.

Why we trust it

We compared 14 harmonization approaches on three very different fire regimes (Ukraine: cropland burning; Brazil: tropical forest and clearing; Australia: savanna and large bushfires) with out-of-sample tests on 2012-2022. Every decision (cell size, monthly multipliers, neighbour borrowing, which satellite builds the series in each period, NOAA-20 equivalence, keeping Terra 2000-2002) is documented with reproducible scripts and evidence pages in the repository. The app shows the uncertainty next to every number: 16-25% per month for areas of 55-220 km.

Benefits and impact

Early warning and emergency services, scientists and land managers get one consistent record from 2000 to today, so they can plan for critical periods, spot unusual seasons and compare years without worrying which satellite produced the data. The interface is built for non-technical users.

Tools and technologies

Python pipeline that downloads and normalizes NASA FIRMS archives (MODIS C6.1, VIIRS Suomi NPP and NOAA-20; 48 yearly archives, about 9.75 GB) and builds the multipliers; PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS serving the harmonized data through SQL functions; Laravel 13 (PHP 8.4) API with a Filament admin panel; Vue 3 + Leaflet single-page app with OpenStreetMap and Esri basemaps; Docker for one-command deployment.

What makes it creative

Instead of one global conversion factor, the multiplier adapts to place and season and openly reports its own error, so users see not only how much burned but also how sure we are.
